items.title: Black Sea bloodshed outstrips Hormuz
items.original_title: Black Sea bloodshed outstrips Hormuz
items.summary: A relentless series of attacks on merchant ships and port infrastructure over the past four days has underscored the Black Sea’s emergence as the world’s deadliest shipping route, with seafarer fatalities this year now exceeding those recorded around the Strait of Hormuz. More than 570 vessels have been attacked in the Black Sea during 2026, with at least 40 seafarers killed, according to figures compiled by maritime security firm Ambrey and the International Maritime Organization and reported by the Financial Times. By comparison, the IMO has confirmed 120 attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East, resulting in 24 seafarer deaths as of October 22. The latest Black Sea violence began on Friday when the Comoros-flagged Khoryv was struck by a drone approximately 13 nautical miles off Romania’s Constanta port. The 43-year-old vessel, sailing from Türkiye towards the Danube port of Sulina, capsized following the strike. NATO has announced additional maritime patrol aircraft, surveillance equipment and drones to strengthen monitoring of the region. The commercial repercussions are becoming increasingly severe. War-risk insurance premiums for some Black Sea voyages have climbed to as much as 15% of a vessel’s hull value, roughly twice the levels reported for the Persian Gulf.

items.title: Panama Canal reopens last-minute slots amid traffic recovery
items.original_title: Panama Canal reopens last-minute slots amid traffic recovery
items.summary: The Panama Canal has restored last-minute transit reservations for ships using its panamax locks, easing one of the restrictions introduced during this year’s drought-related disruption. The canal authority confirmed that the service resumed on October 21, allowing operators to secure short-notice passage when slots become available. The additional reservations will be offered at the authority’s discretion, depending on operational capacity and availability. The easing comes after the canal closed its 2026 financial year with record cargo tonnage. The waterway handled 13,951 vessel transits during the 12 months to September 30, up 4.1% year on year, while tonnage increased 6.5% to 521m Panama Canal measurement tons. Neopanamax traffic accounted for 52.2% of total tonnage, with volumes through the larger locks rising 8.2% compared with the previous financial year. The canal has also been expanding its longer-term reservation arrangements. That programme will cover January 3 to April 3, 2027, providing 288 Panamax slots alongside 270 neopanamax slots through competitive allocations in November. From January 3, 2027, booking swaps and substitutions between shipping alliance members will be extended to vessels in the panamax super category, arrangements previously available only to neopanamax ships.

items.title: EU Proposed SMAP subsidy favors e-fuels and bioLNG
items.original_title: EU Proposed SMAP subsidy favors e-fuels and bioLNG
items.summary: Europe’s carbon market could soon start paying shipowners to switch fuels, but the support on offer is far from equal. In July, the European Commission proposed a revision of the European Union’s Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) that would reserve up to 110 million allowances between 2028 and 2040 for a new Sustainable Maritime Alternative Propulsion (SMAP) mechanism, which is meant to cover part of the price gap between fossil marine fuels and sustainable alternatives. Rystad Energy’s analysis shows that, combined with the EU ETS itself and the FuelEU Maritime regulation, the proposal would reshape the cost ranking of marine fuels in Europe. BioLNG and renewable e-fuels stand to gain the most, while biodiesel made from used cooking oil (UCO) and animal fats – one of today’s most widely used marine biofuels – is left out. SMAP would cover 55% of the remaining price gap to fossil fuel for biogas and advanced biofuels, and 90% for renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBOs) such as e-ammonia and e-methanol, with 10 additional percentage points where the feedstock is sourced in the EU. At 3Q26 prices, bioLNG costs more than twice as much as VLSFO before any incentives, yet it ends up at about half the cost of VLSFO once FuelEU credits and the proposed subsidy are counted.

items.summary: The Trump administration on Friday unveiled its America First Seafood Strategy, outlining plans to strengthen the U.S. commercial fishing industry through regulatory reform, investment in fishing vessels and shoreside infrastructure, and tougher enforcement against unfair foreign competition. The strategy , announced October 23, builds on President Donald Trump’s April 2025 executive order, Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness , and brings together several federal agencies to expand domestic seafood production, modernize processing capacity, and improve market access for American fishermen. The initiative comes as the administration pursues a broader effort to rebuild America’s maritime industrial base, including domestic shipbuilding capacity and the U.S.-flagged fleet. The administration also plans to strengthen the position of American seafood in domestic markets. Trade Representative will also work with other agencies to address unfair foreign trade practices and improve access to overseas markets for American seafood exporters. NOAA said progress will be measured through increases in domestic seafood production and processing, private capital investment, American jobs supported, and reduced dependence on foreign supply chains. The broader goal is to keep more of the economic value of American seafood in the United States, from vessels harvesting fish offshore to the shipyards, processors, and waterfront businesses that support the industry.

items.title: Sanctions risks reshape commodity trading
items.original_title: Sanctions risks reshape commodity trading
items.summary: In the briefing, authors Daniel Martin, HFW partner, and Amanda Rathbone, HFW knowledge counsel (commodities) said that sanctions compliance has evolved from a specialist legal consideration into a central strategic concern for commodity businesses trading oil, gas, metals and agricultural products. Martin and Rathbone warn that the sanctions environment is changing so rapidly that risks can evolve significantly during the lifecycle of a single transaction, from initial negotiations through to shipment, financing and payment. As a result, companies are increasingly being forced to reassess traditional compliance processes and adopt broader, more dynamic risk management strategies. Governments are increasingly using sanctions as instruments of broader geopolitical policy, meaning that ordinary commercial activity and seemingly routine commodity trades can now attract scrutiny. HFW warns that efforts to comply with one jurisdiction’s sanctions requirements can sometimes increase exposure to conflicting regulations elsewhere, creating difficult commercial and legal dilemmas for international trading businesses. The briefing also points to increasing expectations from regulators, who now expect companies to investigate broader sanctions risks throughout a transaction rather than relying solely on screening immediate contractual counterparties against sanctions lists. Martin and Rathbone believe sanctions complexity is unlikely to diminish.

items.title: USTR Proposes Extending China Ship Port Fee Suspension Through January 2027
items.original_title: USTR Proposes Extending China Ship Port Fee Suspension Through January 2027
items.summary: A cargo ship full of shipping containers is seen at the port of Oakland, California, U.S., August 4, 2025. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo The Trump administration is proposing to extend its suspension of port fees targeting China-linked vessels for another two months, pushing their potential return into January 2027 as Washington and Beijing continue negotiations over China’s dominance of global shipbuilding. The proposal, outlined in a Federal Register notice scheduled for publication October 26, would extend the existing one-year suspension through January 9, 2027. Under the proposal, the measures would remain suspended from November 10, 2026, through January 9, 2027. The proposed extension also comes as the administration considers a much broader port fee system under its Maritime Action Plan , unveiled earlier this year. For now, the latest USTR proposal would leave the China-specific port fee measures on hold for another two months, while negotiations continue. USTR has opened a public comment period on the extension, with submissions due by 5 p.m. Comments can be filed through the USTR public comment portal under docket USTR-2026-0694. The notice also does not address whether China will extend its own suspension of retaliatory fees on U.S.-linked vessels.

items.title: Record Tanker Rates Threaten to Push U.S. Oil Exports to Asia to Seven-Year Low
items.original_title: Record Tanker Rates Threaten to Push U.S. Oil Exports to Asia to Seven-Year Low
items.summary: By Yongchang Chin and Nathan Risser (Bloomberg) –US crude oil exports to Asia are set to hit multi-year lows after the Iran war disrupted global shipping and pushed the cost to lease a tanker for the Pacific journey to a record of almost $80 million. Asian refinery orders for US crude for delivery in November tumbled roughly 50% to 24 million to 26 million barrels this month sequentially, according to traders who asked for anonymity because they weren’t authorized to publicly comment. If that pace of orders holds through the end of this month, it would mark a seven-year low, based on ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa. The tanker rate along the US Gulf Coast-to-China route has more than tripled since the US-Iran conflict erupted in late February to almost $60 million as of Thursday, according to Baltic Exchange figures. Those eye-watering rates doesn’t include the cost of the oil itself, which is trading around $100 a barrel. Tanker rates are so inflated that refiners are effectively spending $30 to $35 to haul each barrel of crude from the Gulf Coast to Asia, or as much as seven times what they shelled out last year, Hawkins said.

items.title: Rare Russian Diesel Shipment Expected in Norfolk November 2, Ahead of Tanker Bound for New York
items.original_title: Rare Russian Diesel Shipment Expected in Norfolk November 2, Ahead of Tanker Bound for New York
items.summary: A tanker carrying Russian diesel is expected to arrive in Norfolk, Virginia, on November 2, potentially becoming the first such shipment to reach the United States in more than three years. The Vietnamese-flagged PVT Azura (IMO 9423683), reportedly carrying 109,000 barrels of Russian diesel, departed St. Petersburg on October 15 and is currently signaling Norfolk as its destination, according to VesselFinder . The arrival would come five days ahead of another Russian diesel shipment identified by Reuters on Friday as the first cargo heading to the United States under a recent agreement between President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The tanker has signaled New York as its destination, with an expected arrival date of November 7, although its final discharge port has not been confirmed. The two shipments come as the Trump administration moves to ease restrictions on Russian diesel in an effort to bring down soaring fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. On October 9, Trump announced an agreement under which Russia would immediately supply 300,000 metric tons of diesel to the United States and global markets, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons thereafter.

items.summary: European wholesale natural gas prices surged on Friday, on course to cap the week at their highest levels since late 2022, as an escalation in Middle East military conflict and diplomatic evacuations intensified anxieties over global LNG supply continuity ahead of winter. The benchmark rose 3.8% on Friday to trade at 93.40 euros per megawatt-hour (MWh), locking in a weekly gain of nearly 7%. In Great Britain, the equivalent similarly advanced 3.5% to 229.00 pence per therm, on course to finish the week 6.2% higher. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis launched coordinated drone and missile strikes targeting civilian transport and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including a fatal strike on a civilian airport in Dammam and an attack on ’s Shaybah oilfield. The escalating conflict has severely restricted Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) carrier navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, forcing extended reroutings around Africa and drastically curtailing spot arrivals at European regasification terminals. Benchmark jumped to $114 per barrel on Friday – their highest level in over five months – reinforcing broad-based inflation and input cost pressures across energy-intensive European industries. The weekly surge across European gas curves leaves the continent acutely vulnerable as winter heating demand accelerates.

items.title: Singapore must look beyond the box to secure its logistics future
items.original_title: Singapore must look beyond the box to secure its logistics future
items.summary: Dropping behind Shanghai and Ningbo-Zhoushan in the global container port rankings, and seeing Malaysia’s Port Klang and Port of Tanjung Pelepas nip at its heels should serve as a wake-up call for Singapore, in a changing competitive landscape for box trades For Singapore, this is about more than losing a place in a league table. It is an existential question asking whether a nation built on maritime trade can adapt to a world where supply chain control matters as much as moving containers. As Singapore spent years living off its geographical advantages, deepwater harbour and reputation for efficiency to guarantee continued dominance, its competitors have expanded their infrastructure, attracted manufacturing investment, and developed integrated logistics ecosystems. Part of the problem for Singapore with its nearest rival is that it simply cannot compete with Malaysia when it comes to land availability, meaning it should not focus on warehouses and distribution centres. And the pending Tuas Port, with its planned capacity of 65m teu on full completion in the 2040s, will have a part to play, even if success cannot be judged by volume alone. Yes, the Ministry of Transport’s new Connectivity & Logistics division recognises the need to integrate maritime, aviation, and land transport, but creating a coordinating body will not automatically deliver the commercial agility needed to compete.

Most coverage reads the first as proof that the Arctic is finally opening, but read together, they say something else: the part of the NSR Moscow planned and paid for has missed its targets by a wide margin, while the part it barely planned for has beaten them, because other people’s chokepoints closed. It isn’t that the NSR is missing from an Arctic section; the Arctic silk road itself is absent. I costed the loop the way a carrier’s network team would: a 4,900 teu ship, eight seasonal sailings, west through the Arctic and back via Suez. items.title: Goldman Sachs sees crude freight rates surge to $20 per barrel
items.original_title: Goldman Sachs sees crude freight rates surge to $20 per barrel
items.summary: Global average crude freight rates have climbed above $20 per barrel from $3 per barrel a year ago, according to Goldman Sachs analysis released Wednesday. The increase initially started in the very large crude carrier segment and on Middle Eastern routes before spreading to all major crude trading routes, particularly affecting long-haul voyages. The bank identified five main drivers behind the $20 per barrel year-over-year surge in the average global crude freight rate. A war risk premium in Hormuz accounts for $7 per barrel, representing one-third of the increase in the global average crude freight rate. Inefficient tanker allocation and increased tanker redirections account for $3 per barrel, and the blockage of the Iranian fleet adds $2 per barrel by boosting demand for non-sanctioned crude tankers. Goldman Sachs expects these factors to continue supporting global freight rates as long as the conflict in the Middle East persists. The bank noted that high freight rates may reduce refiners’ overall demand for crude or shift it towards more closely located crude suppliers. Goldman Sachs sees high freight rates widening crude price differentials by changing crude trading patterns and supporting refined product prices while suppressing refiners’ net margins.

items.original_title: US sanctions relief could lift tanker rates in Russia, inject capacity to Gulf shuttles: analysts
items.summary: US sanctions relief on shadow-fleet tankers could redirect ships from Russian oil trades toward the Middle East, potentially raising Russian freight costs while easing some of the tanker shortages around the Strait of Hormuz, shipping analysts said. In recent public remarks, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the US will allow legitimate businesses to acquire sanctioned tankers for non-sanctioned trades to reduce shipping costs, though Washington has yet to announce a detailed relief proposal. The number of oil and LPG tankers sanctioned by Western authorities amounted to 1,226 as of the end of August, with the US having been particularly targeting VLCCs, according to S&P Global Energy Horizons research. But BRS Shipbrokers estimated only 148 tankers in deepsea trades, equivalent to 2.5% of the global total by vessel count, were sanctioned solely by the US Office of Foreign Assets Control as of Oct. That means sanctions relief could redistribute existing tanker capacity rather than simply release large amounts of idle tonnage. BRS said some shadow fleet operators could also use sanctions relief to sell their tankers into the current strong secondhand market, provided Washington gave buyers sufficient assurances that they would not face sanctions risks over the vessels’ previous trading histories.

items.original_title: India’s crude import bill surges 46% to $90.6 billion in April-September on elevated oil prices
items.summary: India’s crude oil import bill surged 46.3 percent to $90.6 billion during April–September on higher global prices even as volumes remained largely flat from the year-ago period, data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) shows. On October 21, Brent crude was trading higher at around $110 a barrel on supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia from Iran-backed Houthi rebels. India imported 122.7 million tonnes of oil during April-September, largely unchanged from 121.8 million tonnes in the previous year. In September, the import bill jumped 46.6 percent to $15.4 billion, while volumes were up 6.8 percent at 21.7 million tonnes. The average price of Indian crude basket has risen to $121.25 a barrel in October from $65.08 from last year. The bigger risk for India is not the availability of crude but persistently higher landed prices that can inflate the import bill, widen the current account deficit and weigh on the broader economy, analysts say. The country imports around 1.8-2 billion barrels of crude annually and every $1-a-barrel increase in price raises the country’s import bill by up to $2 billion a year.

items.original_title: BGN builds up LPG-capable gas carrier fleet with four more ships
items.summary: Energy and commodities trading group BGN has ordered four 93,000-cbm LPG-capable gas carriers from HD Hyundai Heavy Industries for delivery in January 2030. BGN signed the contract for the four very large gas carriers (VLGCs) with South Korean shipbuilder HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HD HHI) in Istanbul. The ships will be able to run on LPG or conventional marine fuel. The new ships will take BGN’s owned VLGC fleet from 19 to 23 once delivered. Including the latest order, BGN has ordered 10 dual-fuel VLGCs from HD HHI in 2026 so far. In April, it ordered four 90,000-cbm dual-fuel VLGCs that can run on conventional and lower-emission fuels and carry ammonia, with delivery by 2029. items.summary: The Panama Canal reported growth in vessel traffic, tonnage and revenue in fiscal year 2026, as stronger demand from energy carriers and containerships helped lift volumes despite ongoing concerns over water availability. The waterway handled 13,951 vessel transits during the fiscal year ended September 30, up 4.1% from 13,404 the previous year, according to results released Wednesday by the Panama Canal Authority. Total tonnage climbed 6.5% to 521 million Panama Canal Universal Measurement System (PC/UMS) tons, compared with 489.2 million tons in fiscal 2025. The results come as the canal continues to balance growing shipping demand with water conservation measures designed to protect operations during the developing El Niño weather pattern. Despite the challenges, the canal maintained a maximum authorized draft of 50 feet throughout the fiscal year’s dry season, providing relatively stable operating conditions for shipping customers. “Far from restricting trade flows, the Panama Canal facilitates international maritime trade by providing its customers with a reliable and safe route,” Panama Canal Administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta said during a conference call hosted by Bank of America Merrill Lynch. The canal has warned that a continuing water deficit could require further operational adjustments, particularly if El Niño conditions intensify.
